findings.title: Cancel imminent reminders immediately instead of waiting for cron
findings.body: Scheduled emails are now only marked cancelled, even when their send time is before the next 15-minute cron run. For example, cancelling a booking five minutes before its reminder sends leaves the email scheduled at SendGrid until after delivery. The cron also deletes past reminders before processing cancellations, so it then discards this cancellation entirely. Reminders close to their send time need an immediate cancellation path.

findings.title: Reschedules still bypass the pending-cancellation limit workaround
findings.body: Every rescheduled booking passes immediateDelete=true, which immediately creates a SendGrid pending cancellation regardless of how far away the reminder is. This retains the 100-pending-cancellations failure described by this PR for reschedules. Furthermore, that branch catches API errors without marking the reminder cancelled, so when the limit is reached the cron cannot retry and the old booking's reminder is still sent. Reschedules should use deferred cancellation with a persisted retry state, except when immediate cancellation is necessary.

findings.title: Persist successful cancellations before another request can fail
findings.body: The cancellation loop accumulates lazy Prisma delete promises and executes them only after every SendGrid request succeeds. If any request fails, execution jumps to the catch and none of the successfully cancelled reminders are deleted. Subsequent cron runs therefore submit those same batch IDs again; an already-cancelled batch can fail and repeatedly prevent later reminders from being processed. Persist each successful cancellation and handle errors per reminder so one failed request cannot block the rest of the queue.

findings.title: Await reminder cancellation database operations before returning
findings.body: The cancellation helpers now perform the database deletion or cancelled-state update themselves, but their promises are discarded inside forEach. Previously the reminder database deletions were included in the awaited Promise.all. The handler can now return successfully before cancellation is persisted, and a serverless request may finish before these operations complete, leaving reminders active. Collect and await both email and SMS helper promises; the same issue occurs in the changed requestReschedule handler.
